narrative.overview:
The site is a workshop after dark: a warm charcoal room, a bench of finished artifacts, and ember task lighting that falls only where someone is working. The darkness is not moody for its own sake — it is what makes the light legible. Ember and flame behave like lamp filaments and solder points: small, hot, and never used as wallpaper.

Density is moderate and rhythmic. Each section opens the same way — a mono label in warm type, a headline pinned to the left edge, a muted sub-line across the page — then fills the bench with a single kind of artifact. Nothing floats free of the ground.

Motion is the workshop's tell: a 30px rise on reveal, spring physics on tilt and press, a magnetic pull on the primary actions. The first viewport establishes the warm ramp immediately — there is no second palette anywhere on the page.
keyCharacteristics: Warm charcoal ground with a subtle 60px grid and two warm glows plus one cold
Ember used as signal, never as fill area; one cool hue reserved for status
Two families with distinct jobs: Instrument Sans speaks, JetBrains Mono annotates
Flat surfaces at rest; shadow reserved for things that float
Pills for controls, 18px cards for artifacts, 28px panel for the contact close

rules.name: The Workbench Rule
rules.body: Warm color marks an active thing — a label, a focus ring, a live control, a hover rule. If warm color is covering more than a small fraction of a viewport, it has become decoration and the design is wrong.

rules.name: The One Ramp Rule
rules.body: Ember and flame are two intensities of one light, not two brand colors. There is no yellow and no second warm hue. The single cool hue (Oxidised Copper) is status, and status is never an action.

rules.name: The Warm Room Rule
rules.body: Neutrals sit at ~15° hue with 0.004–0.013 chroma. A cool grey next to the ember ramp reads as a different room, so surface tints stay warm even when they are almost black.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Instrument Sans speaks; JetBrains Mono annotates. Mono never sets a sentence and sans never sets a section number.

rules.name: The Tight Head Rule
rules.body: Anything at 19px or larger gets negative tracking. Headlines and display at -0.025em.

rules.name: The Sixteen Floor Rule
rules.body: Body copy never drops below 16px on the web. Dense metadata can use the micro step, but a paragraph may not.

rules.name: The Flat-Bench Rule
rules.body: A card that is not floating does not cast a shadow. Raise its fill one step and strengthen its border instead.

dos: Do keep warm color on marks, labels, focus states, and small controls.
Do use the 90px / 70px section rhythm and the shared header pattern.
Do carry depth with a hairline and a one-step fill change.
Do put negative tracking on anything 19px or larger.
Do set numbers and dates in JetBrains Mono with tabular figures.
Do give every interactive control a 44x44px hit area.
Do test every new surface in Arabic RTL.
donts: Don't introduce a third warm hue. Copper is status, not a second accent.
Don't use the warm gradient as a fill.
Don't use Oxidised Copper for a button, link, or focus ring.
Don't add a drop shadow to a resting card.
Don't set body copy below 16px, or set a paragraph in mono.
Don't mix radii — pills for controls, 18px cards, 28px panel.
